newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Carlos" refuses comment in Austrian OPEC probe.
newsitem.headline: "Carlos" refuses comment in Austrian OPEC probe.

text.p: Guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal", now jailed in Paris, declined to comment on Tuesday when an Austrian magistrate quizzed him about the 1975 kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers in Vienna.

Vienna magistrate Georg Olschak, accompanied by an Austrian diplomat, questioned Carlos for about an hour in the Paris law courts in a bid to reconstruct the attack that sealed Carlos' reputation as one of the world's boldest criminals.

But Venezuelan-born Carlos refused to discuss details of the hostage-taking or say who ordered the raid, merely telling Olschak he had nothing against the Austrian people and that he respected then-chancellor Bruno Kreisky, judicial sources said.

Olschak refused at the end of the meeting to shake Carlos' hand, saying he did not want to repeat a controversial 1975 handshake by the Austrian interior minister after providing the guerrillas with a getaway plane to fly to Algiers.

The meeting, in the office of France's top anti-terrorism magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere, was an attempt to piece together the attack on December 21, 1975 when Carlos stormed the OPEC headquarters in Vienna with five heavily-armed guerrillas.
It was the first time Carlos, whose real name is Ilich Ramirez Sanchez, faced an Austrian inquiry. Most of the interview was in English.
The guerrillas killed three people -- an Austrian policeman, an Iraqi and a Libyan -- in the raid as OPEC ministers including Saudi Arabia's Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani dived under tables.

They seized 81 hostages, including 11 ministers. After freeing all 41 Austrian hostages, they flew to Algeria on a commandeered Austrian DC-9. After a trip to Libya and then back to Algiers, the remaining hostages were freed on December 23.
Algeria let Carlos and his guerrilla companions go free.

It is unknown who was behind the kidnappings. Investigators say Carlos may have been acting on the orders of Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi to punish OPEC members like Saudi Arabia and Iran for being too pro-Western and not militant enough towards Israel.
Carlos, who often fought for the Palestinian cause, said at the time his gang was called "Arm of the Arab Revolution". The Vienna raid was disowned by the Palestine Liberation Organisation.

Carlos, 48, has been held in La Sante jail since he was seized in Sudan in 1994 and brought to France. He refuses to cooperate with foreign investigators, saying they are part of a back-up plan by France in case its own trial plans collapse.
He is to go on trial for the first time on December 12 for the murder of two French counter-intelligence officers several months before the OPEC attack in 1975.

Carlos' lawyer, Frederic Pariente, said he would seek his client's acquittal. "He denies it and there are no witnesses," he said. Carlos is also under investigation for a series of other attacks in France.
Carlos lashed out at Bruguiere during Tuesday's questioning, accusing the authorities of intercepting and delaying all his mail, even to family or lawyers.
